description: Cross-language porting matrix for GPU compute engines. Maps constructs, types, memory patterns, and ABI boundaries between C++, Python, Rust, and other languages.

cpp.name: C++20

numeric_types.bf16: __nv_bfloat16 (CUDA), __hip_bfloat16 (HIP), std::bfloat16_t (C++23) — NO native on RDNA2, EMULATE on gfx1030

kernel_dispatch.hip_launch: hipLaunchKernelGGL(kernel, grid, block, shared_mem, stream, args)

cpp.abi_boundary: extern "C" — no name mangling, C calling convention. Use for Python ctypes / Rust FFI.
cpp.strict_notes: All GPU kernels compile as CUDA or HIP language. C++ host code uses MSVC or GCC/Clang. Must use --fmad=false / -ffp-contract=off for bit-exact parity. Windows needs Windows SDK paths.

python.name: Python 3.10+

numeric_types.f16: numpy.float16 — NOTE: no arithmetic, must cast to f32
numeric_types.bf16: ml_dtypes.bfloat16 — third-party, no native numpy support

memory.cuda_free: obj.gpudata.free() / cupy.ndarray goes out of scope

kernel_dispatch.torch_custom_op: torch.autograd.Function — registers C++ backend via pybind11

python.abi_boundary: ctypes — load C++ shared library, call extern "C" functions. Or pybind11 for richer bindings.
python.strict_notes: Python floats are f64 by default — MUST cast to f32 for parity. No control over FMA contraction (must use numpy.seterr + careful). No GPU memory management API — relies on GC or explicit free().

porting_from_cpp.cuda_free: Call .gpudata.free() explicitly, or let GC handle it
porting_from_cpp.cuda_kernel_launch: kernel_func = mod.get_function('name'); kernel_func(args, block=(x,y,z), grid=(x,y,z), stream=stream)
porting_from_cpp.extern_C: Load .dll/.so via ctypes.CDLL — bind extern "C" function name

porting_to_cpp.tensor_ops: Use ggml/s2_gemv kernels directly — no numpy equivalent
porting_to_cpp.managed_memory: cudaMallocManaged — but note: on AMD, hipMallocManaged may fall back to staging
porting_to_cpp.autograd: Must implement backward pass manually in C++ kernels
porting_to_cpp.dtype: Python float → C++ float (f32). Python int → C++ int64_t. numpy types map to C++ int types via ctypes
porting_to_cpp.framework_extraction: To port Python/Torch/Triton kernels to standalone C++ without Torch runtime: 1) Use `triton.compile()` to get PTX/AMDGCN binary. 2) Disassemble to LLVM IR. 3) Extract kernel body as CUDA/HIP C++ intrinsics. 4) Wrap in extern "C" for C++ linkage. 5) Link against raw CUDA/HIP runtime (no Python deps).

torch_to_cpp.description: Extract CUDA/HIP kernels from PyTorch/TorchInductor generated code
steps: Run `torch.compile(..., mode='reduce-overhead')` to generate Triton/CUDA kernels
Extract kernel body → write as standalone .cu/.hip file
Replace torch.tensor args with raw float*/void* pointers
Compile standalone with nvcc/hipcc — no torch dependency
gotchas: torch.compile inserts CUDA graphs for some kernels — extract individual kernels
Generated Triton code uses tl.* — map to CUDA intrinsics manually
Autograd backward must be re-implemented as separate kernel

triton_to_hip_cpp.description: Extract standalone HIP C++ from Triton kernels
steps: Map AMDGCN instructions to HIP intrinsics (v_mad_mix_f32 → __builtin_amdgcn_fma_mix_f32, etc.)
Create standalone .cpp file with `__global__` kernels using HIP intrinsics
triton_to_hip_cpp.note: Triton→HIP via upstream `third_party/amd` backend (2025+). See triton-lang/triton/issues for coverage.

rust.name: Rust 1.80+

numeric_types.fp8: No standard crate — use raw u8 + manual bit manipulation

kernel_dispatch.rust_cuda: ptx crate + #[kernel] / launch!(kernel, grid, block, args)

rust.abi_boundary: extern "C" block — declare extern functions from C++/.dll/.so. Use bindgen to auto-generate bindings.
rust.strict_notes: No official ROCm/HIP bindings — must use FFI or write custom HIP shim. rust-cuda targets NVIDIA only (PTX path). For AMD, link against libhip and call hip* FFI functions.

porting_from_cpp.cuda_kernel_launch: kernel.launch(grid, block, shared_mem, stream)(args) — via cuda-runtime-sys FFI
porting_from_cpp.extern_C_to_Rust: extern "C" { fn cudaMalloc(...); } — wrap in safe Rust types
porting_from_cpp.struct_layout: repr(C) on structs passed to GPU kernels — must match C++ layout

porting_to_cpp.ownership: Rust owns its memory; map to C++ via RAII or explicit free
porting_to_cpp.error_handling: Rust Result<T> → C++ optional<T> or expected<T, E> (C++23)
porting_to_cpp.lifetimes: No equivalent in C++ — must document ownership rules in comments
porting_to_cpp.zero_cost_abstraction: Rust iterators → C++ templates; verify compiler inlines

cuda_pty.name: PTX (virtual ISA)
cuda_pty.description: Virtual assembly. Stable across NVIDIA GPU generations. JIT-compiled to native SASS by the driver.
cuda_pty.porting_notes: PTX is the most portable target on NVIDIA — emit PTX instead of cubin for forward-compatibility. --ptxas-options=-v shows register usage.

hip_isa.name: HIP (AMD/NVIDIA)
hip_isa.description: Single-source C++ for AMD and NVIDIA. Uses ROCm for AMD, can target NVIDIA via hipNVCC backend.
hip_isa.porting_notes: HIP headers via hip_compat/ shim. __HIP__ macro selects HIP paths. roc-clang generates code objects for gfx targets.

spirv.name: SPIR-V (Vulkan/OpenCL)
spirv.description: Standard intermediate representation for Vulkan and OpenCL. Cross-vendor.
spirv.porting_notes: No compute engine currently uses Vulkan (Maya is CUDA/HIP only), but SPIR-V is the portable option for multi-vendor GPU compute. Requires Vulkan loader + driver.

cross_port_matrix.description: Quick reference: how to translate between language constructs

C++.to_Python: Use ctypes to call extern "C" functions. Use pycuda for GPU kernels. Cast numpy arrays to raw pointers via .ctypes.
C++.to_Rust: Keep extern "C" interface, use bindgen to generate Rust FFI. Wrap in safe Rust types.

Python.to_C++: Use pybind11 to embed Python in C++, or rewrite kernels as extern "C" and call via ctypes.
Python.to_Rust: Use pyo3 for Rust extension modules, or rewrite as Rust binary calling CUDA FFI.

Rust.to_C++: extern "C" interface. Use #[no_mangle] on export functions.
Rust.to_Python: Use pyo3/maturin for Python extension, or call Python via PyO3.

strict: 1. Map all numeric types (f32/f16/bf16/fp8/i8) — verify no precision loss
2. Map memory management (malloc/free ↔ RAII ↔ GC ↔ ownership)
4. Verify ABI boundary — extern "C" must match name mangling
5. Verify struct layout — repr(C) in Rust, #pragma pack in C++
6. Map FMA contraction behavior — Rust f32::mul_add vs C++ fma() vs numpy default
7. Map rounding mode — nearest-even is default, but CUDA has __fmul_rn
8. Verify parity test passes before performance work
loose: 1. Verify types map (f32 → f32, f16 → float16, etc.)
2. Verify memory management strategy matches (manual ↔ GC ↔ Drop)
